toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Don't send the breach notice. The best explanation is the tag stock change, not the handler. On 1 September Harlow Bay check-in moved to Fennick tag stock. Corvane tags printed on it fail automatic reading 11.8% of the time, against 1.5% for August's Brackwater tags. Transfer and Pelion tags stayed around 1.3–1.4%, so the airport's readers are not the problem. On 14–16 Oct, counters briefly used Brackwater stock from stores and those tags failed at only 1.6%. Kiosk tags printed on the same days failed at 12.1%. Unreadable tags go to the manual encode desk and reach the laterals after they close. That fits the late-bag comments Tessaly made.

I can't yet say whether the Fennick stock is defective or whether the printers just need different heat settings. No printer settings changed, and no test data on either stock was collected. Inexperienced Tessaly crews may add some mishandling, but they don't explain the doubling.

Next steps: return counters and kiosks to Brackwater now (about five weeks of stock is on hand, and the contract runs to 31 Dec). Then test Fennick stock with adjusted printer settings before any claim against Fennick. Hold the breach notice and fee withholding. Confidence is fairly high, about 80%.
output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe-style specification (IS/IS NOT on tag range), then ACH across five hypotheses, with a provenance check on sources with a stake in the outcome; EDF record kept throughout.
